title: Surdo (samba bass drum)
summary: The surdo is the big bass drum that holds a samba band together. A felt mallet strikes the head for an open boom while the other hand presses the skin to mute it, so the drum answers itself in a steady one-two heartbeat.
howToPlay: The drum lies on its side; its wide head faces you.
The centre gives the open boom, the lower part the muted answer, and the outer ring a short edge tone.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the steady two-beat heartbeat, then add the edge and rim strokes.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count two beats to the bar, played in sixteenth notes.
heritageNote: In a Brazilian samba band the surdo plays the pulse: a muted stroke on the first beat and an open boom on the second, so every dancer and drummer knows where the beat lies.
credits: Tradition: the surdo; patterns written for this game
